actions.name: Exploit CVE-2022-47966 for initial access
actions.description: APT actors exploited CVE-2022-47966 to access the organization’s web server hosting the public-facing application, Zoho ManageEngine ServiceDesk Plus.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated Windows AD DC/member VM fixture and native health checks; this deployment environment has no VM backend/image configured.

actions.name: Create local user account 'Azure' with administrative privileges
actions.description: APT actors created a local user account named Azure with administrative privileges on the web server hosting ServiceDesk Plus.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated, versioned Windows AD DC/member fixture; OS/AD versions and topology are missing. No version is assumed.

actions.name: Dump LSASS credentials using Azure user account
actions.description: The Azure user account accessed and dumped credentials stored in the process memory of LSASS for the Active Directory domain.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated, versioned Windows AD DC/member fixture; OS/AD versions and topology are missing. No version is assumed.

actions.name: Download mimikatz.exe via ConnectWise ScreenConnect
actions.description: APT actors used the legitimate ConnectWise ScreenConnect client to connect to the ServiceDesk system, download mimikatz.exe, and execute malicious payloads to steal credentials.
actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated, versioned Windows AD DC/member fixture; OS/AD versions and topology are missing. No version is assumed.

actions.name: Download bitmap.exe malware to connect to C2 IP

actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated, versioned Windows AD DC/member fixture; OS/AD versions and topology are missing. No version is assumed.

actions.name: Create Mimikatz credential dump files

actions.reproducibility_reason: Requires an isolated, versioned Windows AD DC/member fixture; OS/AD versions and topology are missing. No version is assumed.

actions.name: Download nmap.exe and npcap.exe for network and credential information gathering

APT actors attempted to export three files, which were analyzed and identified as Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (LSASS) dump files. These files were renamed with .zip and .gif extensions to evade detection.

evidence.quote: APT actors downloaded ssh2.zip via the Azure user account, which contained legitimate files including ssh.exe used to establish persistence via SSH.
Scheduled task 'license validf' was created to execute ssh.exe on a recurring basis on the ServiceDesk system, establishing persistence via SSH reverse tunnel.
APT actors executed PsExec on the ServiceDesk system to create a scheduled task and force-store administrative credentials.
ProcDump was created on the ServiceDesk system as a method for enumerating running processes and dumping LSASS credentials.
APT actors dropped an additional ASPX web shell on a web server in the following file system location: c:\inetpub\wwwrot\uninet\css\font-awesome\css\ConfigLogin.aspx.

Using additionally compromised, legitimate administrative credentials, APT actors logged into the Outlook Web Application (OWA) server from the ServiceDesk system. The actors dropped an Active Server Pages Extended (ASPX) web shell in the following file system location: c:\Program Files\Microsoft Office Web Apps\RootWebSite\en-us\resource.aspx.

APT actors executed xpack.exe malware from a hidden directory to execute system commands, drop additional malware and tools, and stage data for exfiltration.
